items.title: Noah Cook Interview, 1960-08-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] But do you think you would have gotten along better with North? No. [INTERVIEWEE] I thought, no. That's the question he asked me. I told him, no.

ctx.x: I was a carpenter. I was a carpenter. I made carpenter the second year after I did that. I was a carpenter. I was surprised I got there, I didn't stay. I'd have been a child if I stayed, if I didn't stay. See, I was a non-commissioned officer the second year after I got there. And we used to have a non-commissioned officer school every Wednesday. And I used to ask, you see, an elected man can't do no talking to officers. He can't, he said, that's all he can do to shoot your officers and go. He can't do no…
But do you think you would have gotten along better with North? No.

I thought, no. That's the question he asked me. I told him, no. I didn't think he'd get along any better with Captain. I said, here's what I figured. I said, the, the, the, the blueback book tells us what we have to do towards the office, and the office has got to tell us what we got to do towards ourselves. So, therefore, it wouldn't be no better. It would be the same thing, but I just wanted to know. That's all. I said, the book guides the army. He said, that's right. The book guides the army. Now, in, in, uh,…
